ai.description: This 3–4 cm toad is dark brown with irregular black mottling. It is distinguished by its flattened body, warty skin, and lack of a tympanum. It inhabits rocky crevices in Meghalaya, India.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bufoides meghalayanus* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of prominent, fleshy, leaf-like dermal appendages on its eyelids and limbs, which are absent in other toads.
ai.habitat: The Khasi Hill Rock Toad inhabits rocky crevices and stream banks within subtropical broadleaf forests at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 1,500 meters in Meghalaya, India.
ai.behavior: The Khasi Hill Rock Toad is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by wedging its flattened body deep into narrow rock crevices to evade predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bufoides meghalayanus* is oviparous, breeding during the monsoon (May–August). Females lay small clutches of eggs in rock crevices or water-filled tree holes.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bufoides meghalayanus* is endemic to the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, where it inhabits rocky stream environments at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Khasi Hill Rock Toad emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard echoing from rocky crevices near cascading mountain streams.
